Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

democracy noun

also a democracy, democratic, rule of the people

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.42
Plin. NH 7.200
M-O s.v. form: democracy

cīvitās populāris

noun phrase: cīvitās, cīvitātis f., with the adjective populāris

a democracy

Cicero’s name for the state in which all power lies with the people, beside rule by a king (rēgnum) and by the best men (optimātēs); Pliny sets it against rēgia cīvitās, monarchy. Democratic is populāris (Lewis & Short). Levi and Bini (p. 21) add ratiō populāris for the system and lībera rēs pūblica for democracy in its better sense.

Examples

  • illa autem est cīvitās populāris (sīc enim appellant), in quā in populō sunt omnia

    and that is a democracy, as they call it, in which everything is in the hands of the peopleCic. Rep. 1.42

  • rēgiam cīvitātem Aegyptiī, populārem Atticī post Thēseum

    the Egyptians (invented) monarchy; the Athenians, after Theseus, democracyPlin. NH 7.200

Other words

  • dēmocratia, dēmocratiae f. — democracy

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Serv. ad Aen. 1.21 (M-O s.v. form: democracy); Traupman 179, 302

    Greek δημοκρατία. Not in Lewis & Short; Morgan–Owens cites Servius and Dante, and Traupman gives it.

See also republic, political, government, state.
